newsitem.title: UK: UK's Oftel eases BT equipment regulation.
newsitem.headline: UK's Oftel eases BT equipment regulation.

text.p: UK telecoms regulator Don Cruickshank said on Wednesday British Telecommunications Plc need only supply him with information on cross subsidies of its 'phone equipment businesses on a quarterly basis rather than a monthly one.
The move is part of Cruickshank's drive to reduce unnecessary regulation, but the watchdog said that he would remain vigilant in monitoring BT's performance.

"My aim is to see the telephone equipment market become fully competitive," he said. "As always, if the need arises, I will not hesitate to take enforcement action. I hope that I will not have to do so."
Cruickshank imposed a direction in BT's licence in 1995 to stop cross subsidies in businesses including the supply of telephones and faxes to ensure that they made an adequate return.
He charged that the company's Network Application Business was unfairly subsidised or cross subsidised by other, more profitable parts of BT's business operations, which could harm competition.
However, from April 1, BT has exited rental markets for cordless telephones, answering machines and faxes.
The subsidy tests, however, remain in respect of other rental equipment, Cruickshank said in a statement.

BT is not allowed to dispose of any excess fax machine stock which has accumulated, or account for stock returns or obsolete stock in a way which Cruickshank deems would disrupt retailers' businesses.
BT will meet the subsidy tests over rolling periods of 12 months starting on July 1 and on each subsequent quarter.
